Форк Belobug теперь показывает 5–7 кадров в секунду на Radeon RX 9070 XT (ранее было 3–5): 5,4–6,7 в статике в сцене с 8400 объектами, меньше при езде. Его README объясняет прирост тем, что игре позволяют возвращать данные до завершения работы видеокарты, а также использованием памяти игры напрямую вместо копирования. Его «скоростная полоса» переходит на 3-й этап, проект поднимается на 4-е место.

BRVIctory-ka1qux включил собственную трассировку лучей в игре по умолчанию — это первая публичная сборка на этой странице с такой настройкой. Его README гласит, что это стоит 0,05–0,1 секунды на кадр; проверка проводилась только на одной улице открытого мира в четырех заездах по 5–11 минут без вылетов.

Прогноз был пересмотрен в 17:24 UTC и оставлен на уровне около суток. Аргументы «за»: три кодовые базы теперь сообщают о 10 кадрах в секунду в ранних сценах, количество отчетов от сборок и машин растет каждый час, а README от VIctory подтверждает, что в игру можно зайти. Аргументы «против»: эти цифры — лучшие показатели, мейнтейнер victory-fork утверждает, что данные форка получены в статичной сцене, трансляция шейдеров игры теперь стоит дороже, чем сам слой, и ни одна длительная сессия не показала в среднем 10 кадров. Отчет, опубликованный к 22:00 UTC, остается в силе, и если к этому времени не появится отчетов о 15 кадрах в игре или 10 кадрах вне первых интерьеров по результатам долгого прогона, прогноз сдвинется на четверть суток вперед. Ни Rockstar, ни Take-Two не давали комментариев с момента утечки сборки.

updates.title: Собственный README от VIctory теперь подтверждает, что в игру можно зайти, а victory-fork уточняет свои 10 кадров в секунду.
points: README от VIctory (16:51 UTC) теперь открывается фразой «Пока не играбельно, но в игру можно зайти». Сообщается, что вступительная кат-сцена проигрывается, а начальная миссия достижима с полностью отображаемой графикой при 1 кадре в секунду на Radeon RX 6700 XT: текстуры и освещение есть, без теней от трассировки лучей и непрямого света. Его «полоса картинки» переходит с 1-го на 2-й этап.

Мейнтейнер victory-fork добавил ограничение в 16:54 UTC к цифрам, опубликованным здесь в 15:38 и 16:19 UTC: 9,6 и 10,3 кадра в секунду — это показатели для статической сцены. Пока камера движется, игра подгружает ассеты, и около половины времени уходит на кадры длительностью 490 мс, в течение которых видеокарта простаивает около 330 мс. README не упоминал об этом, когда писалась последняя запись на этой странице. Его «скоростная полоса» теперь показывает 2–12 кадров, прогноз остается без изменений до следующего планового пересмотра.

README от BRVIctory-ka1qux сообщает, что собственное освещение с трассировкой лучей теперь можно включить в качестве опции на BRVIctory-ka1qux Radeon RX 7800 XT: затененные здания, деревья и персонажи получают отраженный свет, что добавляет около 0,05 секунды на кадр. Было проведено три сессии по 5, 6 и 11 минут без вылетов. Это третья публичная кодовая база с подобным отчетом после DexNom Runtime и пул-реквеста в victory-fork; по умолчанию опция отключена.

README от Kelvaroq теперь сообщает, что управление персонажем, HUD и пауза подтверждены в игре, а время тяжелых кадров снизилось до 108,5 миллисекунд. Инцидент в GitHub все еще был открыт в 16:57 UTC, а Pages работали с частичными перебоями, поэтому эта страница может обновиться с задержкой.

updates.title: victory-fork преодолевает отметку в 10 кадров в секунду в первых локациях, к таблице присоединяются еще две сборки.
points: README от victory-fork (16:19 UTC) показывает в первых локациях 97 миллисекунд на кадр (10,3 кадра в секунду) с тремя изменениями, которые по умолчанию отключены. Также подсчитано время работы видеокарты: около 50 из 87 миллисекунд занятости приходятся на собственные проходы игры в транслированном виде, поэтому даже при удалении каждого прохода самого слоя сцена все равно выдавала бы около 20 кадров, к тому же транслированные шейдеры должны стать менее ресурсоемкими. Показатель получен в первых локациях, поэтому ни одна из отметок, опубликованных с оценкой, не достигнута, и оценка остается прежней.

Две сборки присоединяются на 6-м этапе, каждая со своими показателями с одной машины. Kelvaroq, с аккаунта, опубликовавшего Palmwave, сообщает, что вступительная миссия играбельна при частоте около 10 отрисованных кадров в секунду в типичных сценах и 7–8 кадров в самых тяжелых при выводе в 4K на RTX 5080, согласно замерам в 5-минутных сессиях. victory-unified, объединяющая наработки четырех форков, сообщает о 2 кадрах в секунду на RTX 3070 с 8 GB и одной сессии длительностью 49 минут 42 секунды; такая длительность сессии оставляет ее на 3 шага ниже планки «Играбельно».

README от vilocity теперь выдает от 3 до 7 кадров в секунду в первой локации на RTX 5080 (ранее было от 2 до 5) после отключения шумоподавителей для проходов трассировки лучей, которые не работают. Скоростной показатель переходит на 3-й этап, обходя BRVIctory-ka1qux.

TechRadar сообщил 25 ноября, что в некоторых сборках вступительная глава играбельна при нескольких кадрах в секунду, что далеко от планки этой страницы. С момента утечки сборки от Rockstar или Take-Two не поступало никаких заявлений. Статус-страница GitHub показывает инцидент с 15:55 UTC, который затрагивает Pages и операции Git, из-за чего два развертывания этой страницы завершились неудачей, поэтому обновления могут прийти с задержкой.

updates.title: victory-fork показывает 9,6 кадра в секунду в первых локациях, основная ветка VIctory снова обновляется, к таблице присоединяются две сборки.
points: README от victory-fork (15:38 UTC) показывает в первых локациях 104 миллисекунды на кадр (9,6 кадра в секунду) с двумя изменениями, которые по умолчанию отключены (утром того же дня было около 120). Сообщается, что поток отправки слоя и видеокарта полностью загружены, поэтому оптимизация только одного из них меняла время кадра на 0–7%, а консольный показатель в 33 миллисекунды все еще недостижим. Показатель ниже обеих отметок, опубликованных с оценкой, которая остается прежней.

Мейнтейнер VIctory отправил 82 коммита в основную ветку в 15:46 UTC — первые с 01:36 UTC: загрузка текстур теперь происходит пакетами и только при изменении их байтов, оптимизировано отслеживание памяти и исправлены шейдеры. README все еще выдает 1–2 секунды на кадр.

Две сборки присоединяются на 6-м этапе. CBL VIctory, о которой спрашивали в 14-м тикете в репозитории этой страницы, сообщает о сессии длительностью 27 минут 38 секунд на RTX 5080 при 3,6–6,4 кадра в секунду в зависимости от сцены (сессия была завершена вручную после того, как предыдущая вылетела на 20-й минуте); это собственные данные с одной машины, и сборка находится на 3 шага ниже планки «Играбельно». Doomsday — это приватная сборка, которую PortWatch, по его словам, проверил с включенным освещением с трассировкой лучей при 3–5 кадрах в секунду и почти без вылетов. Это слова PortWatch, а не самой группы, и код не является публичным.

README от VItoriaBr теперь сообщает, что кожа, ландшафт, растительность и тени работают с использованием затененного заменителя окружающего освещения, взятого из форка Belobug, при частоте до 6 кадров в секунду на RTX 5060 Ti. На этом основании показатель графики переходит со 2-го на 4-й этап.

updates.title: Таблицу можно фильтровать по системе, производителю видеокарты и этапу.
points: В каждой строке теперь указано, на каких системах и видеокартах, по отчетам проекта или тестировщиков, запускается игра. Она может работать и на другом оборудовании.

Ссылка «Filter the table» над таблицей позволяет сузить список строк по системе, производителю видеокарты и минимальным значениям на каждом этапе, например, по длительности сессии от 30 минут и более. Позиции сохраняют свои номера при скрытии строк. Это предложили читатели в тикетах 12 и 13 в репозитории этой страницы.

updates.title: Разработчик приватной сборки сообщил о письме от Rockstar, а Flamingo зафиксировал 24-минутную сессию с частотой 8.6 кадра в секунду.
points: VGTimes сообщает, что разработчик приватной сборки, указанной здесь как omonkey, получил письмо от Rockstar и прекратил стриминг работы, пообещав дальнейшие обновления. Письмо не было опубликовано, а Rockstar не дала комментариев. Это первый подобный случай, зафиксированный здесь.

Лог запуска Flamingo показывает 24-минутную игровую сессию: от самого начала до выхода в город, со средней частотой 8.6 кадра в секунду в открытом мире на RTX 4070. Это самый высокий средний показатель для сессии длительностью от 20 минут, полученный на одном устройстве и пока не подтвержденный; он всё ещё ниже отметки 10, требуемой для следующего этапа.

Открытый пул-реквест в victory-fork сообщает о работе системы построения трассировки лучей в игре на протяжении 7 минут; она отключена по умолчанию, так как требует около 88 миллисекунд на кадр. VIniVIdiVIci переходит из списка наблюдения в таблицу на 5-й этап: согласно README, в открытом мире игра выдает от 3 до 5 кадров в секунду на RTX 4060 Ti, ввод данных пока не тестировался.

Прогноз: оценка остается на вечер четверга, 26 ноя. Днем появились новые сборки, сессия с прохождением новой игры до открытого мира и эксперименты с трассировкой лучей, но ни один показатель в игре не превысил 14 кадров, а основной код victory-fork не обновлялся с 12:43 UTC. Новости: заявлений от Rockstar или Take-Two не поступало, уведомлений о других проектах нет.

updates.title: DexNom Runtime запускает трассировку лучей в игре в экспериментальном режиме, а klbf-lab добирается до открытого мира в новой игре.
points: Отчет о тестировании DexNom Runtime (14:52 UTC) гласит, что с включенным экспериментальным режимом игра компилирует и выполняет структуры трассировки лучей в открытом городе на Radeon RX 7900 XTX с частотой около 1 кадра в секунду, при этом освещение отдельных объектов еще не проверено. PortWatch сообщает, что видела работу освещения с трассировкой лучей в этой сборке, и переместила её на первое место в своем рейтинге в 14:56 UTC.

README от klbf-lab (14:55 UTC) сообщает об игре с начала до открытого мира на собственных сохранениях: первые две миссии, затем свободное перемещение с частотой около 5–8 кадров в секунду во время езды и ходьбы в течение 77-минутной сессии, о которой сообщалось ранее. Она остается на первом месте.

vilocity переходит из списка наблюдения в таблицу на 6-й этап: согласно README, вступительные кат-сцены и первая комната работают с частотой 2–5 кадров в секунду на RTX 5080, со сбоем графического драйвера примерно через 7 минут. AnyXboxX сообщает о 23-минутной сессии без вылетов на Linux на Radeon RX 9070 XT, пройдя начальную миссию с медианой 3.7 кадра в секунду.

Прогноз не изменился. Трассировка лучей при 1 кадре в секунду не приближает нас к планке 20, а ни один отчет пока не достигает 15 кадров в игре или 10 вне первых интерьеров. Основной код victory-fork не обновлялся с 12:43 UTC.

updates.title: DexNom Runtime присоединяется к таблице после того, как PortWatch поставил его на второе место в своем рейтинге.
points: PortWatch добавил DexNom Runtime, форк VIctory для видеокарт AMD Radeon, в свой рейтинг на второе место в 14:34 UTC. Сообщается, что сборка работает на уровне Belobug's: открытый мир близок к розничной версии игры, миссии проходятся с частотой около 3–4 кадров в секунду.

Собственный отчет о тестировании форка показывает 3.5–4 кадра в секунду в помещениях на Radeon RX 7900 XTX с сохраненной игры, при этом освещение интерьеров всё еще некорректно, а длительность сессии не указана. Согласно правилам этой страницы, он попадает на 6-й этап, до планки «Играбельно» не хватает 6 шагов.

Страница статуса five-star-recomp сообщает, что запуск проработал 18 минут в открытом мире без сбоя графического драйвера, как только были ограничены проходы трассировки лучей. Изображение мира всё еще отображается только в красных тонах.
VIctory-macOS сообщает, что время отрисовки кадров в мире на M5 Pro сократилось с 4.5 секунд до примерно 2.4–2.9 секунд. Основной код victory-fork не обновлялся с 12:43 UTC, прогноз не изменился.

updates.title: VIctory-Belobug-AMD затеняет свой временный источник света, а IGN запрашивает комментарий у Take-Two
points: README от VIctory-Belobug-AMD (14:00 UTC) сообщает, что имитация трассировки лучей теперь слабее в складках и под объектами, а собственные тени от солнца и ламп в игре работают. По-прежнему фиксируется от 3 до 5 кадров в секунду на Radeon RX 9070 XT, около 380 вызовов отрисовки за кадр отбрасываются, а производительность упирается в работу процессора.
VIctory-macOS сообщает, что текущий код позволяет находиться в игровом мире более 20 минут без зависаний на M3 Max при 0,1–0,2 кадра в секунду. Никто еще не дошел до геймплея на Mac.

Новости: IGN сообщил о требовании об удалении и заявил, что запросил комментарий у Take-Two. С момента утечки сборки заявлений от Rockstar или Take-Two не поступало, а в списке GitHub нет уведомлений с упоминанием других проектов.

VIniVIdiVIci, форк victory-fork, протестированный на RTX 4060 Ti, добавлен в список наблюдения по просьбе читателя. В его README указано, что результаты собственного игрового процесса еще не опубликованы. Прогноз остается прежним: вечер 26 ноя.

updates.title: klbf-lab проходит вторую миссию до конца, к таблице присоединяются два форка, а прогноз сдвигается на четверть дня раньше
points: README от klbf-lab (13:47 UTC) сообщает о прохождении вступительной миссии и всей второй миссии до конца за одну 77-минутную сессию без вылетов на новейшей тестовой сборке на Radeon RX 9070 XT со средним показателем около 5,2 кадра в секунду и около 9 во время полета. Указано, что внутриигровые сохранения работают, а растительность становится пурпурной и земля остается очень темной ночью.

Два форка victory-fork присоединяются к таблице на 6-й стадии, основываясь на данных из README для каждой машины. Flamingo сообщает о первой геймплейной сцене неназванного тайтла при 9–12 кадрах в секунду на RTX 4070 в пониженном разрешении, около 14 в самых легких сценах, за 15-минутные сессии, и занимает второе место в списке. BRVIctory-ka1qux сообщает о 25-минутной игровой сессии и 6,6–6,9 кадра в секунду в стабильных сценах открытого мира на Radeon RX 7800 XT.

Прогноз сдвигается на четверть дня раньше, на вечер 26 ноя, до которого осталось чуть больше суток. Отчет Flamingo — второй, где достигнуто 10 или более кадров в игре, со второй машины после victory-perf, что является условием, опубликованным на этой странице в 10:36 UTC. Оба отчета получены из самых легких сцен, новейший код Flamingo выдает 9–10 кадров, а обычный геймплей в других местах — 5–9 против 20, требуемых для планки «Играбельно», поэтому сдвиг небольшой.

Что повлияет на прогноз дальше. Раньше на четверть дня: 15 или более кадров в игре на любой машине или 10 или более вне первых интерьеров по результатам длительной сессии. Позже на четверть дня: эти показатели отозваны или опровергнуты, получено требование об удалении с упоминанием VIctory, victory-fork или их сборки, либо ни одна из ранних отметок не подтверждена обзором около 22:00 UTC 25 ноября.

updates.title: Тестовая сборка klbf-lab проходит полет на гидросамолете, а вторая видеокарта подтверждает исправление воды
points: README от klbf-lab (13:12 UTC) сообщает, что в новейшей тестовой сборке лодка, взлет гидросамолета, полет при 9 кадрах в секунду и посадка на воду во второй миссии работают на Radeon RX 9070 XT. На этой сборке миссия еще не пройдена до конца.
Сообщается, что другой пользователь подтвердил исправление воды на RTX 5070 Ti в своей собственной сборке. klbf-lab остается первым в списке 6-й стадии, в 2 шагах от планки «Играбельно».

Основной код victory-fork не менялся с 12:43 UTC. В открытом пул-реквесте сообщается, что игра проработала 74 секунды с включенным построителем структур трассировки лучей, тогда как раньше она вылетала через несколько секунд; на экране пока ничего не изменилось.
VIctory-macOS сообщает, что текущий код загружается в мир на M5 Pro без зависаний при 0,2 кадра в секунду (ранее 0,1). Никто еще не дошел до геймплея на Mac.

updates.title: Stage 6 is now ordered by a published rule, and klbf-lab moves to first
points: Until now the order inside a stage was this page's own judgement. From this check the 13 rows at stage 6 are ordered by their lanes and nothing else: fewest steps short of the playable bar on speed and stability together, then the better picture, the higher frame rate and the longer session. The key under the standings title states the rule, and each row shows its count.

Speed is now read as the middle of the frame rates a project reports in play, where it was the best of them, so a best-case scene no longer sets the step. victory-perf's 4.5 to 14 reads as step 3 of 6, down from 4, and VItoriaBr's 3.5 to 6 as step 2, down from 3.

The order today: klbf-lab, victory-fork, AnyXboxX, ztrx, VIctory-Belobug-AMD, victory-perf, omonkey, victory-amd, suri, VItoriaBr, ScarlettPort, CGBJ and VIctory. klbf-lab and victory-fork are level at 2 steps short, and klbf-lab's picture is a step better. A project that reports no run length counts as having none, which is why VItoriaBr and ScarlettPort sit lower than before.

The rule reads only what projects report about themselves, on different cards and scenes, and it does not count how far into the story a build has been played. Stages below 6 have no lanes and are still ordered by this page's reading.

updates.title: Correction: victory-fork withdraws the 8.9 frames a second reported here, and gives 7 to 8
points: At 12:20 UTC this page reported victory-fork's first room at 6.0 frames a second by default and 8.9 with a newer draw path. At 12:43 UTC the project withdrew both figures: its README says the two runs stood in different scenes and could not be compared.

Its corrected figures come from one run each on an RTX 4070. At the same load a frame takes 145 ms with the newer path off and 124 ms with it on and memory copies made in place, about 6.9 and 8.1 frames a second. On screen it reports 7 to 8 in the first rooms and 10 to 12 in lighter views.

The same notes describe a first play session past the first rooms. It reached the open world and lost the graphics device there in about 13 minutes, with the 12 GB card out of room for new textures, and the cause is not known.

The estimate does not move: the gain is smaller than first stated, ordinary play is still under 10 frames a second, and nothing was withdrawn as unstable. Also in this check, ScarlettPort reports its frozen overlay fixed, still at about 4 frames a second, and VIctory-macOS reports its loading freezes on Macs fixed.

updates.title: Rows at stage 6 now show three lanes: picture, speed and stability
points: Thirteen projects sit at stage 6, so each of their rows now carries three more meters. Speed is the best average the project reports in play, stability is the longest session it reports without a crash, and picture follows written steps. The key under the standings title lists them, and blue marks the steps that meet the playable bar.

On speed, the front of the field is at step 3 of 6, from 5 to 9 frames a second: victory-fork at 8.9, klbf-lab at 8.4 and AnyXboxX at 6.9. victory-perf's unconfirmed 9 to 14 reads as step 4. Playable asks for step 5, 20 frames a second.

On stability, klbf-lab and ztrx report sessions of more than an hour, and victory-fork's code and AnyXboxX pass the 30 minutes the bar asks for. On picture, VIctory-Belobug-AMD and one private build read as lit and whole, and most of the others still have black or dark shadows.
The lanes were suggested by a reader in issue 8 on this page's repository.

updates.title: victory-fork merges a third batch of frame-rate work and measures 8.9 frames a second in its first room
points: victory-fork's maintainer merged a third batch of frame-rate work at 12:06 UTC. On the maintainer's RTX 4070 the first room averages 6.0 frames a second by default, up from 4.5 to 5 two hours earlier, and 8.9 with a newer draw path switched on, from one run each. The opening cutscene went from 3.1 to 4.2.

The notes say that draw path stays off by default: of eight runs with it on, one lost the graphics device 44 seconds into the world for a reason not yet found. They also say the regular dips in earlier measurements came from the test harness and not the game, and that the merged tree's whole test suite was not run.

The estimate stays at late on Thu 26 Nov. 8.9 is the highest figure merged so far, but it comes from one run on one machine and is short of the 10 frames a second in play, from a long run or a second machine, that this page set as its next mark. An open pull request on the same code reports 131 to 139 ms a frame by default, about 7.2 to 7.6 frames a second.

klbf-lab's test page reports a median of 6.6 to 8.4 frames a second in the world at reduced resolution on a Radeon RX 9070 XT, in runs of 14 minutes, and an optional frame generation mode that shows about 17 from about 8.5 rendered. This page counts rendered frames only, and its notes now say so. TuxBox's longest recorded run on Linux is now 18 minutes 11 seconds, with the opening cutscene still not appearing.

updates.title: klbf-lab's boats float in a test build, and Belobug's fork draws vehicles and distant trees whole
points: klbf-lab's README, updated at 11:51 UTC, says a newer test build fixes the water physics that stopped the second mission: with only the throttle held, the boat floated and moved for over a minute before hitting the bank. The project says a full play-through comes next, and the fix is not yet in the version it recommends.

VIctory-Belobug-AMD's README, updated at 11:41 UTC, now lists moving vehicles as whole and distant trees as drawn, both broken before. It lists the in-game phone as broken, some draws dropped in the heaviest places, and about 33 GB of memory committed after a quarter of an hour's drive. Its frame rate is unchanged at 3 to 5 frames a second on a Radeon RX 9070 XT.

An open pull request on victory-fork measures a small gain on an RTX 4070, in a scene it does not name: sending fetches to a copy queue by default took the frame from 180 to 192 ms down to 174.5 ms, about 5.7 frames a second. It is not merged, and victory-fork's main branch is unchanged since 10:20 UTC.

keylime moves from the watch list into the table at stage 5, in 25th place, on its README's report of the intro, main menu and loading screen at 30 frames a second, with no test machine named and no outside report. VIctory-macOS now reports a dark city skyline on an M5 Pro at 0.1 frames a second and says nobody has reached gameplay on a Mac.

updates.title: klbf-lab plays further into the second mission, and one more fork joins the table
points: klbf-lab's README, updated at 11:04 UTC, reports play from the opening mission into the second as far as a seaplane, in a 41-minute session on a test build without a crash, at 5.2 frames a second on average and 12.9 at peak on a Radeon RX 9070 XT. Menus, the map and the HUD now show in that build. Boats, the seaplane and the player in water behave as if there were no water, so those parts were skipped, and the project says it has found the cause and is testing a fix.

victory-amd, a fork of victory-fork with fixes for AMD Radeon cards, joins the table at stage 6 in 12th place. Its README reports the opening cutscene and the first room with the player moving at 2 to 3 frames a second on a Radeon RX 7800 XT, in runs of about 8 minutes, tested on one machine.

VIctory-macOS reports the game reaching the world on a second Mac, an M5 Pro, as a grey screen at 0.1 frames a second, and loading at 26 to 30 frames a second instead of 8 with new patches. Two projects written from scratch join the watch list: keylime reports the intro, main menu and loading screen at 30 frames a second with no picture in the opening cutscene yet, and gta-vi-astral reports the game running its loop with no 3D picture yet.

Forecast review: the estimate stays at late on Thu 26 Nov. klbf-lab's 12.9 is a peak and its average is 5.2, no report reaches 10 frames a second in play from a long run or a second machine, and victory-fork's main branch is unchanged since 10:20 UTC. No new takedown notice names a listed project, and the hourly news sweep found no statement from Rockstar or Take-Two beyond the notice against Leonida.

updates.title: Three more public projects join the table, two of them in-game
points: klbf-lab, a build of VIctory and victory-fork, reports the player in control from the opening mission to the start of the second on a Radeon RX 9070 XT at reduced resolution: 5.7 frames a second while playing, 7.3 standing still over 72 minutes, and 74 minutes in one session without a crash. Its README calls the figures self-reported from one machine. It enters at stage 6 in third place.

VIctory-Belobug-AMD, a fork of VIctory for AMD Radeon cards published at 09:41 UTC, reports the world lit and textured at 3 to 5 frames a second on a Radeon RX 9070 XT, with moving vehicles broken and a flat stand-in for ray-traced light. PortWatch, whose owner reports having seen it, ranks it first on its own scale and says it looks close to the retail game. Its README says it is not playable yet. It enters at stage 6 in fourth place.

Port of the Americas, a Linux layer, joins at stage 5: its press-start screen, setup pages and loading screens draw, and its world is still black. five-star-recomp's status page says the opening shot's 3D world now reaches the screen through the final composite, in red only. XCL merged 35 pull requests into its main branch between 10:40 and 10:51 UTC with no change to its stated status.

The estimate does not move. None of the new figures reaches 10 frames a second in play, and they sit in the same 3 to 7 range as the rest of the field. They add to the evidence that the picture and stability are no longer what holds a playable build back.

updates.title: victory-fork merges a measured frame-rate gain, and the estimate moves a quarter of a day earlier
points: victory-fork's maintainer merged a second batch of frame-rate work at 10:20 UTC. On the maintainer's RTX 4070 the first room went from about 3.5 to 4 frames a second to 4.5 to 5 by default, and to 6 to 7 with every new switch on. The change that lost the graphics device earlier is now in, off by default, with five runs since its fix and no loss.
The notes say frame-rate dips remain with no known cause, and that the merged tree's whole test suite was not run. The figures come from one machine and one room.

The estimate moves a quarter of a day earlier, to late on Thu 26 Nov, about a day and a half away. A measured gain merged into victory-fork is one of the conditions published at 09:17 UTC. The gain is on a mid-range card and far short of 20, so the move is small. It moves earlier again on 10 or more in play from a long run or a second machine, and later if the gain is withdrawn as unstable or a takedown notice names one of these projects.

Builds that take victory-fork's code are picking the work up. ScarlettPort now reports about 4 frames a second in the opening mission on an RTX 3060, up from 2.6, with a frozen overlay over the picture, and VItoriaBr reported up to 6 on an RTX 5060 Ti at 10:10 UTC.

updates.title: VItoriaBr reports up to 6 frames a second, and PercyScarlett reaches the opening scene
points: VItoriaBr's README, changed at 10:10 UTC, reports the open world at 3.5 to 6 frames a second on an RTX 5060 Ti with no driver timeouts, where it gave about 3 before. It had merged victory-fork's 07:30 frame-rate work and several community fixes from 09:31 UTC. It is the first tracked build to publish a gain since that work landed, on a mid-range card, and it is still below the 7.6 measured in a long run on an RTX 4090.

PercyScarlett released a v1.0 whose runtime is now built on VIctory, victory-fork and ScarlettPort. Its README says it reaches the opening scene of a title it does not name, lit and textured, at about 2 to 3 frames a second on an RTX 2060 SUPER at reduced resolution, and that speed is far from playable. It says nothing about control there, so it stays at stage 5 and moves to the top of that group, 11th.

The estimate does not move. Neither figure reaches 10 frames a second, nobody has confirmed victory-perf's, and victory-fork's own main branch has not moved since 07:30 UTC. The conditions published at 09:17 UTC stand.

News check: no statement from Rockstar or Take-Two since the build leaked, and no notice naming another project. VideoCardz has picked up the story, reporting gameplay at 2 to 5 frames a second in unofficial builds and saying projects are moving into private development after the takedown. Of the public repositories this page tests, all but Palmwave still answer.

updates.title: Estimate held at its mid-morning review
points: The mid-morning review leaves the estimate at early on Fri 27 Nov. This was the check for moving it a quarter of a day later if speed had not moved. It has started to: victory-fork merged its first frame-rate work at 07:30 UTC, and its notes name the cost that remains and a change that more than halves it but is not yet stable.

It does not move earlier either. Nothing measured in a long run has beaten about 7.6 frames a second since 22:15 UTC on 24 November. victory-perf's 9 to 14 in interiors is still one unconfirmed report, the only other reduced-resolution measurement is 6.1 to 6.4 on an RTX 3090 Ti, and XCL has reported neither control nor a longer run.

What moves it next. Earlier by a quarter of a day: a second report of 10 or more in play, a confirmation of victory-perf's figures by someone else, or a measured gain in frame time merged into victory-fork. Later by a quarter of a day: those figures withdrawn or contradicted, or none of the three by the review at about 13:30 UTC.

News check: nothing new. Neither Rockstar nor Take-Two has commented since the build leaked. Today's coverage, heise's included, reports the Leonida takedown from the notice GitHub published. No notice names another project, and no outlet has covered or tested victory-perf.

updates.title: VIctory-macOS reports the game world on screen on a Mac
points: VIctory-macOS's README, changed at 08:25 UTC, says that in a later run on one tester's M3 Max the game world appeared on screen before the game's own watchdog stopped it, with frames taking up to 28 seconds while shaders compiled. It is this project's first report of the world on screen on a Mac. It says nothing about control, so it stays at stage 5 and moves up one place to 13th, and the README still says the game is not playable on the Mac.

Nothing has moved at the front. victory-fork's main branch is unchanged since 07:30 UTC, VIctory's since 01:36 UTC and XCL's world branch since 07:45 UTC. New pull-request measurements on victory-fork stay at about 4 frames a second on an RTX 3090 Ti, and victory-perf's figures are still unconfirmed.

updates.title: ScarlettPort joins the table, and a second reduced-resolution measurement comes in under 7 frames a second
points: ScarlettPort, a public build of victory-fork's code that this page had not listed, reports the lit world at about 3 to 4 frames a second on an RTX 3060 at reduced resolution, with the keyboard walking the character. Its README does not name the title and says nobody has played a session end to end. It enters the table at stage 6 in sixth place. victory-perf credits it for some of its code.

A victory-fork pull request measured the game's lower-resolution mode on an RTX 3090 Ti: 6.1 to 6.4 frames a second, steady, in the opening mission, against 4.7 to 4.8 at full resolution. That supports the direction of victory-perf's report but not its 9 to 14, which nobody else has confirmed. The estimate does not move.

News check: neither Rockstar nor Take-Two has commented since the build leaked. TweakTown's report that the Leonida takedown is confirmed rests on the notice GitHub published, and no notice names another project. GameGPU describes footage, credited to a post on X, of boat gameplay on open water at 3 to 5 frames a second, which matches what builds listed here report. No outlet has tested or covered victory-perf.

XCL's unmerged world branch gained 17 commits on memory mapping and device handling, with no new frame rate, run length or word on control. victory-fork's main branch has not moved since 07:30 UTC and VIctory's since 01:36 UTC.

updates.title: A new fork reports 9 to 14 frames a second in interiors, and victory-fork merges its first frame-rate work
points: victory-perf, a fork of victory-fork published on the morning of 25 November, reports the opening mission's interiors under player control at 9 to 14 frames a second on an RTX 4070 SUPER, and 4.5 to 6.5 in heavy scenes. The figures are its maintainer's own, from one machine at reduced resolution, with no run length given and shadows lit by stand-ins, and its heavy-scene figure matches what AnyXboxX already reports on the same card. It enters the table at stage 6 in fifth place until someone else confirms it. It calls those scenes playable, which they are not by this page's bar of 20 frames a second held for 30 minutes.

victory-fork's maintainer merged the fork's first frame-rate work at 07:30 UTC. One processor-side pass fell from 70 to 220 ms a frame to about 3, but the frame is still 250 to 380 ms on an RTX 4070 because, in the README's words, "the card is the limit now". A change the maintainer tried cut the card's time from 100 to 150 ms a frame to 35 to 80, lost the graphics device twice and was left out.

The estimate stays at early on Fri 27 Nov. These are the first signs of speed moving since 22:15 UTC on 24 November, but the best figure from a long run is still about 7.6 frames a second and the new ones are unconfirmed. A second report of 10 or more in play, or a measured gain in frame time merged into victory-fork, would move it earlier. The mid-morning check will weigh these reports before moving it either way.

Also on 25 November: VIctory-macOS reports the picture showing on one tester's M3 Max as far as the opening title card, where the game froze, and enters the table at stage 5. five-star-recomp says the opening shot's 3D world now draws into an off-screen buffer and does not reach the screen yet. TuxBox published a second machine's run record, in which the game reported itself running for 12 minutes 45 seconds with loading artwork on screen before a crash.

updates.title: Leonida Continued joins the table, and the estimate holds at its review
points: Leonida Continued, a continuation of the halted Leonida that this page has listed under Watching as leonida (ubiquitarianism), changed its README at 07:04 UTC. It now says the game boots on Windows and on Linux through Proton, shows the launch movie, the first-run pages and the landing prompt, which respond to a controller, then runs the story load to its end and enters what it calls the world phase.

By its own account no frame of the world has been verified on any test machine and nothing is playable. Its test report covers about 80 starts on a Linux machine with an RTX 4070 and runs on a Windows machine with an RTX 4070 Ti, and lists a lost graphics device at the start of the world among the things that stop it. It enters the table at stage 5, recognisable picture.

Forecast review: the estimate stays at early on Fri 27 Nov. No speed gain has been merged in the VIctory family, the best figure measured in play is still about 7.6 frames a second, and new measurements in victory-fork pull requests come in at about 4.3 at best on an RTX 3090 Ti and an RTX 4090. The check for moving it a quarter of a day later comes mid-morning in Europe, at the review due at about 09:30 UTC.

News check: nothing new. Neither Rockstar nor Take-Two has commented since the build leaked, no outlet has confirmed the reported notices over footage with Take-Two, and GitHub's list shows no notice naming another project. Palmwave's repository is still not answering.

updates.title: victory-fork: the first room renders right, and the frame rate is where it was
points: victory-fork's maintainer merged another batch at 06:46 UTC. The README now says the first room renders right on the test machine, with walls, textures, people and lamps, at 190 to 450 ms a frame, which is 2 to 5 frames a second. In its words, the picture work has caught up and the frame rate has not.

The notes credit two fixes taken from VIctory and from pull requests, and say the processor now compares 25 MB a frame for shader writes where it compared 550 to 710 MB. A change that saves 3.1 GB of the card's memory ran on a card for the first time and stays off by default. One five-minute run had no device loss, and the merged tree's test suites were not run.
Its headline status still says 2.5 to 4 frames a second with shadowed areas black. The best figure measured in play is unchanged at about 7.6 frames a second, so the estimate does not move.

updates.title: XCL corrects its figure: about 5 frames a second in the world, not 14
points: XCL's README, changed at 06:23 UTC, now gives about 5 frames a second in the 3D world on an RTX 5090. Its commit note says the 14 it published at 04:53 UTC was the average of a whole 5-minute run with menus and loading included, and that the world ran at 5 to 6. It has lowered its own progress estimate from about 65 to about 60 percent.

This page reported the 14 at 05:01 UTC as a whole-run average and did not count it as a frame rate in play. XCL's world figure now sits alongside the VIctory family's 3 to 7.6. The rest of its report stands: the picture of the world is incomplete, runs there are short, and it does not say whether the player has control.
Elsewhere: victory-fork's main branch has not moved since 05:44 UTC, and VIctory's has not moved since 01:36 UTC. No new takedown notice has appeared in GitHub's list.

updates.title: Take-Two is reported to be sending takedown notices over footage of unofficial builds
points: VGTimes and Twisted Voxel report, citing a post on X by the reporter Ben, that Take-Two is sending takedown notices over social media posts that show footage of unofficial PC builds. By VGTimes' account, one notice says the port is being developed from leaked copies of Rockstar's files and that the footage contains Rockstar's characters, environments and other material.

Neither report names a platform, a number of notices or a project, and neither carries a statement from Take-Two. It is the first reported action since the notice against Leonida. No new notice has appeared in GitHub's public list.

Neither company has commented since the build leaked. Before launch, Take-Two's chief executive said piracy would be met with legal and technical measures, and called unofficial PC ports made with AI a creative concern more than a financial one.

Projects: XCL's world branch has 12 more commits and no new figures. Two victory-fork pull requests report every ray-traced shadow program now translating, which is not yet ray-traced lighting in the game. Speed is unchanged.

updates.title: victory-fork's main branch gets memory fixes; no change in speed
points: victory-fork's maintainer merged memory fixes at 05:44 UTC. A write to a memory page that the game shows at several addresses now reaches every copy of it, which the notes say happened 0.8 to 1.0 million times in a five-minute run. The first room now has its walls in the later frames of four runs out of four, against two of five before.

The notes report five 5-minute runs on an RTX 4070 without a device loss and give no new frame rate. They say the test card's memory is full from the first frame of the world, and that a fix for it is written but switched off and not yet run on a card.
Nothing else moved. VIctory's main branch is unchanged since 01:36 UTC, XCL's world branch is still unmerged, and the best figure measured in play is still about 7.6 frames a second.

updates.title: Estimate reviewed and held at about 2 days; testers' reports back XCL's route into the world
points: Routine review of the estimate at 05:22 UTC: unchanged at about 2 days. XCL's report adds a second, independent route into the game's world, but it gives no frame rate in play, no player control and no long runs. In the VIctory family, the best figure measured in play has been about 7.6 frames a second for over seven hours.

A community-run board that tallies testers' reports on XCL's pull requests, last updated at 00:44 UTC, lists five reports of the world on screen and one of a tester playing by hand at about 6.9 frames a second in a short run. The board says these counts are not confirmed.

What would move the estimate: earlier if XCL reports control, a frame rate in the world or a longer run, or if a speed gain is merged in the VIctory family; later if neither has happened by mid-morning in Europe.
News check: no statement from Rockstar or Take-Two, no takedown notice naming another project, and no press coverage yet of XCL's report or of builds past the opening mission.

updates.title: XCL reports its 3D world, at 14 frames a second on average over a short run
points: XCL's README, updated at 04:53 UTC, says that with a branch not yet merged the newer retail game it does not name goes on from its menus into its 3D world on an RTX 5090. It gives 4,307 frames in a 300-second run, which is 14 frames a second on average, and about 5 in the heaviest scene.

The README does not split that run between the menus, which run at 30 frames a second, and the world, so 14 is not a frame rate in play. It calls the game not playable: the picture of the world is incomplete, with its minimap and other mesh pipelines refused, and it does not keep running there for long. It does not say whether the player has control.
XCL is a separate code base from VIctory and its forks, so this is a second route into the game's world. It stays at stage 5 here until it reports control, and moves ahead of five-star-recomp.
The estimate is unchanged for now and is due a routine review at about 05:30 UTC. The best figure measured in play is still about 7.6 frames a second, from the VIctory family.

updates.title: Speed work in the pull-request queues: a large gain on a synthetic test, smaller ones measured in the game
points: An open pull request on victory-fork changes how the layer tracks the memory the game writes, and reports a drop from 390 ms to 9.8 ms a frame on an idle RTX 4090. That figure comes from a test program its author wrote, not from the game: the author says no game files were on the test PC. Its effect on the game has not been measured.

Measured in the game: an open pull request on VIctory cuts the graphics time of a world frame on an RX 9070 XT under Proton from 600 to 720 ms down to 150 to 310 ms, and one on the fork takes an RTX 3070 laptop card in Series S mode from 353 ms to 305 ms a frame.

None of these is merged, and none is a new top speed: the best measured figure in play is still about 7.6 frames a second. News check at 04:20 UTC: no statement from Rockstar or Take-Two, and no new takedown notice.

updates.title: XSXEmu starts the game's code on a Mac without Wine; correction on TuxBox's stage
points: XSXEmu's README now says the game's own code runs under Rosetta on Apple Silicon, starts its worker threads and opens its archives. It has not created a graphics device, run a shader or produced a frame, and it says no game is playable. It stays on the watch list.

Correction: the 02:09 UTC update said TuxBox stays at stage 4. TuxBox has been at stage 5 on this page since 23 November, when it showed the player-selection prompt, and the standings showed stage 5 throughout. The earlier line is fixed.

Nothing new on speed. victory-fork's main branch has not changed since 03:19 UTC, and VIctory's has not changed since 01:36 UTC. More than 510 pull requests have now been opened against the fork, and a new one reports and fixes a fault that ran parts of the ray-tracing structure builder up to 64 times more than asked.

updates.title: victory-fork's main branch moves again; estimate reviewed and held at about 2 days
points: victory-fork's maintainer merged texture fixes at 03:19 UTC, the first change to its main branch in two hours. The notes say the first room now shows its walls and the characters' textures on a first launch, and put speed at about 3 to 5 frames a second. They add that more than half of the card's texture memory is held for detail levels the game has not loaded, which is the next job.

Routine review of the estimate at 03:30 UTC: unchanged at about 2 days. Stability has three reports beyond the bar, so speed is the gap. The best measured figure in play has been about 7.6 frames a second for over five hours, most of them overnight in Europe, while more than 500 pull requests have now been opened against the fork. That is too short a pause to move the estimate later, and nothing has happened to move it earlier.

One clue on speed for common cards: an open pull request on the fork measures the graphics time per frame in the first room at about three times higher on an 8 GB card once its texture memory runs out.

Press: no statement from Rockstar or Take-Two has appeared in any coverage found. The Verge reported the Leonida takedown on 24 November, and by Make Tech Easier's account it names VIctory and its forks as the projects in front. Notebookcheck relays unverified Reddit claims that more Discord servers have been removed.

updates.title: Scarlight narrows to Linux on AMD and restates its speed; a fork joins the watch list
points: Scarlight's README now describes it as a port for Linux on AMD RX 9000 cards first, and says it does not support NVIDIA cards or native Windows. Its candidate build, on victory-fork's code, shows the opening mission's world lit at 2 to 3 frames a second at best on an RX 9070 XT, with many runs at 1 to 2. The earlier README said about 1 to 4. The build is not merged into its main branch.

Added to the watch list: project-flamingo, a fork of VIctory that Scarlight's README points NVIDIA and Windows users to. Its README still carries VIctory's status from 23 November and reports no results of its own.

An open pull request against victory-fork reports all 52 programs of the game's ray-tracing structure builder translating on an RTX 3060 laptop card, up from 49. Its author says the builder then writes outside its buffers and the game faults, so ray-traced lighting is still missing.
PortWatch now ranks ztrx first on its board, saying the build has not crashed between the opening mission and the second. Speed is unchanged everywhere: about 7.6 frames a second at best in play.

updates.title: AnyXboxX's maintainer sees 7 to 8 frames a second in cutscenes
points: AnyXboxX's README now says its maintainer saw a steady 7 to 8 frames a second during cutscenes, with peaks at 9, read from the window caption on an RTX 4070 SUPER. In one scripted run the medians measured from the log were lower, at 2 to 3 frames a second depending on the scene.

These are cutscene figures, and the two methods disagree. Its measured figure for the world under player control is unchanged at 5.3 to 6.9, so the top measured speed in play stays at about 7.6 frames a second and the estimate does not move.

Nothing else changed in status. victory-fork's main branch has not moved since 01:22 UTC while more than 470 pull requests have been opened against it, VIctory's main branch has not moved since 01:36 UTC, and Palmwave remains unreachable.

updates.title: AnyXboxX relays a report of the first two missions completed
points: AnyXboxX's README now says a contributor played for about 45 minutes at about 2 frames a second and completed the first two missions. The maintainer relays the report and did not measure it from the project's own logs.

The maintainer reports every cutscene playing in full, and measures 5.3 to 6.9 frames a second on an RTX 4070 SUPER with its newest mix of victory-fork and fifteen of that project's pull requests. The mix no longer needs the Microsoft library it tried earlier. Ray-traced lighting is still off, and some graphics are missing in places.

It is the furthest into the game that any public project has reported. Speed at the top is unchanged: about 7.6 frames a second at best, against the 20 that playable needs, so the estimate stays where it is.

updates.title: TuxBox gets into the story intro on Linux
points: TuxBox, which is not built on VIctory, reports a Linux run under Proton getting into the story intro by the game's own state after 9 minutes 41 seconds, then crashing. Until now it had stopped at the player selection prompt.

It says the game is not playable: many shaders are unsupported, and the picture, input and frame times in the intro are not yet checked. It stays at stage 5 here, where it has been since it showed the player-selection prompt on 23 November. This line first said stage 4 and was corrected at 04:00 UTC on 25 November.
No new speed figures elsewhere. More than 430 pull requests have now been opened against victory-fork, whose main branch has not changed since 01:22 UTC.

updates.title: VIctory's main branch gets a speed change; correction on palmetto's origins
points: VIctory's maintainer merged a change at 01:36 UTC that stops the runtime re-checking memory the game's shaders did not write. Its notes put the old cost at 0.45 to 0.7 seconds of a 1.5 to 1.7 second frame in the opening cutscene. The README's figure of 1 to 2 seconds a frame is not yet updated.

Correction: palmetto's commit history, public again since about 01:45 UTC, says the repository descends from the project network that received Take-Two's notice, and that references to the game and to that project were removed in response. This page said at 22:22 UTC that its files did not show that origin.
five-star-recomp reports most of the opening cutscene's 3D passes now running. Its 3D world is still not visible, and long runs end in a GPU hang.

Open pull requests on victory-fork and VIctory report fixes that let the game's ray-tracing structure builder run on NVIDIA cards and that restore material colours that came out black. Neither is merged.

updates.title: A public build reports the whole opening mission played, in a session of over 90 minutes
points: ztrx, a build of victory-fork's code published at 01:11 UTC on 25 November, reports in its README the opening mission playable from start to finish on an RTX 3050 with 8 GB, in one session of more than 1 hour 30 minutes without a crash. It runs at 1 to 3 frames a second, and anything in shadow is black.

It is the first public code to make that claim and the longest session reported by anyone. PortWatch, which first listed it as a private build, says it verified the build going on into the next mission.

A second public build of the same code, VItoriaBr, joins the standings. Its README reports the opening scenes at about 3 frames a second on an RTX 5060 Ti and says the world is not yet playable, while PortWatch reports its live stream reaching the second mission at up to 4 frames a second.

victory-fork's main branch now runs at about 4.3 frames a second on an RTX 4070 by default, up from about 2.5, and lights its first room for the first time. The estimate moves in by a quarter of a day, to about 2 days: stability now has two long reports, and speed is the only gap left.

updates.title: Estimate reviewed and left at about 2½ days
points: The estimate was reviewed at 01:05 UTC on 25 November and is unchanged: about 2½ days, around midday on Fri 27 Nov. The highest reported rate has not moved since 22:15 UTC, about 7.6 frames a second on an RTX 4090, while mid-range cards have caught up to 6 or 7. Playable needs 20.

PortWatch now says it has verified one private build playing through the opening mission into the next, at about 2 frames a second with poor rendering. That speaks to how well the game runs, not how fast, so it does not move the estimate.
No takedown notice names a front-runner. Palmwave's repository has been unreachable for nearly three hours, for reasons that are not known.

updates.title: PortWatch reports private builds getting past the opening mission
points: PortWatch's owner reports that several private builds now play through the opening mission and load the next one, the furthest into the story anyone has reported. The report names no builds and cites no recordings, and says most appear to build on victory-fork.

By the same report most of them still render the world badly and vehicles mostly do not work, so the next mission cannot be played properly. PortWatch has not changed its scores, and no public project claims this.

victory-fork's main branch gained a fix for characters' faces and hair that came out black or pale in about three launches of four. The cause was textures uploaded before the game had filled them. Its README is unchanged.

updates.title: VIctory merges about 130 pull requests, and Scarlight shows a lit picture on Linux
points: VIctory's maintainer merged about 130 pull requests into its main branch between 00:20 and 00:23 UTC on 25 November, the first movement there in nearly three hours. Its status line is unchanged: the world is drawn at 1 to 2 seconds a frame, unlit. The lighting and speed changes this page has reported from its open pull requests were not in the batch.
victory-fork's main branch changed for the first time since 20:45 UTC, taking two contributors' branches: a fix for AMD cards and support for more shader instructions. Its README is unchanged.

New entry: Scarlight, based on VIctory and aimed at AMD cards on Linux. Its README reports the opening scenes lit at about 1 to 4 frames a second on an RX 9070 XT under Proton, on a branch built on victory-fork. Its main branch still shows a mostly black world.
Decrypt reports that Rockstar did not respond to its request for comment on the removal of Discord servers. No outlet carries a statement from Rockstar or Take-Two.

updates.title: AnyXboxX measures up to 7.1 frames a second with an optional mode
points: AnyXboxX added an optional mode that hands texture layout to Microsoft's own library, which the user must supply from a development kit and which is not in its repository. With it the maintainer measures 5.4 to 7.1 frames a second on an RTX 4070 SUPER, against 5.1 to 5.6 without, over about 3 minutes 40 seconds with no device loss.

The highest rate reported anywhere is still about 7.6 frames a second, on an RTX 4090 in an open pull request on victory-fork. More than 280 pull requests have now been opened against the fork, whose own main branch is unchanged.

updates.title: AnyXboxX's newest mix gets the indirect-light shaders running
points: AnyXboxX now runs victory-fork with eight of that project's open pull requests. The added one makes the two shaders behind the game's indirect light translate, the ones without which everything outside direct light stayed black, and its maintainer reports their pipelines created and bound in game. Its notes do not yet claim a picture with lit shadows.
It measures 4.8 to 5.4 frames a second on an RTX 4070 SUPER, over about 4 minutes 20 seconds without a device loss. Ray-traced lighting is still absent.

An open pull request on victory-fork cuts a frame with the ray-tracing structure builder switched on from 3.3 seconds to 0.55 seconds on an RTX 5080. More than 250 pull requests have now been opened against the fork, whose own main branch is unchanged.

updates.title: An 8 GB card reaches 6 to 7 frames a second in a pull request on the fork
points: An open pull request on victory-fork reports 5-minute runs in the world on an 8 GB graphics card at about 155 milliseconds a frame, 6 to 7 frames a second, up from 4 to 4.5, with no crash. It is the author's own measurement and is not merged.

That is close to the 7.6 frames a second reported on an RTX 4090 an hour earlier. More than 210 pull requests have now been opened against the fork, whose own main branch has not changed in effect since 20:45 UTC.
PC Gamer's explainer on the race, published at 21:47 UTC, says a recompilation could run within days and warns that many circulating clips look fake. It quotes no statement from Rockstar or Take-Two.
XValkyrie published a bundled copy of the VIctory engine at about 23:00 UTC and had removed it from its history 20 minutes later.

updates.title: A 30-minute run is reported on the fork, and the estimate moves in to about 2½ days
points: An open pull request on victory-fork reports a 30-minute run in the world without an error or crash on an RTX 4090, at about 132 milliseconds a frame, or about 7.6 frames a second. It is the author's own measurement, the change is not merged, and it does not say how much of the run was under player control.
It is the longest session and the highest frame rate reported so far. Playable here needs 20 frames a second for 30 minutes, so the gap left is speed, and the estimate moves in by a quarter of a day.

Other open pull requests on the fork report the world drawing lit on an AMD RX 9070 XT, the lower-resolution Series S mode drawing the opening cutscene on an 8 GB RTX 3050 at 0.4 to 1.2 seconds a frame, and 36 of 40 ray-tracing programs translating on an RTX 5080.

PortWatch lists a new private build, suri, built on victory-fork: about 3 frames a second in the first scene, with a picture PortWatch calls close to the retail game. It joins the standings here as a private build, on PortWatch's word.

updates.title: Correction: palmetto is back, with a new history
points: palmetto's repository answered again by 22:17 UTC, after about 25 minutes offline. Its history was replaced: five commits starting at 22:07 UTC where there had been 37, with folders renamed. Its link here is restored.
Its reported state is unchanged: the title boots, executes its draws and presents frames in its own window, and the picture is black.
This page had called it a continuation of Leonida, following a community list. The project's own files do not say that, so the label is removed.

updates.title: Palmwave stops answering; ray-tracing and lighting fixes arrive as pull requests
points: Palmwave's repository stopped answering between 21:52 and 22:17 UTC. No published takedown notice names it and the reason is not known. palmetto's return shows that a repository can go quiet without a takedown.

An open pull request on victory-fork reports four of the five shadow-ray programs and the ray-tracing structure builder now translating on graphics cards where they had been kept off. It claims no picture yet, and the fork's README is unchanged.
An open pull request on VIctory traces the black, unlit world on NVIDIA cards to buffer reads that return zeros, and proposes a fix. It is not merged.

Tom's Hardware, heise online and Dexerto now cover Leonida's shutdown. Tom's Hardware and tbreak quote no statement from Rockstar, Take-Two, Discord or GitHub, and tbreak, citing Decrypt, reports a GTA VI modding Discord server removed and others locked down. GitHub published three more takedown notices, none about these projects.

updates.title: VIctory's own code now shows the world, and the fork is reported on AMD cards
points: VIctory's README, updated at 21:36 UTC, now says the first mission's world is drawn and shown, with streets, buildings, vehicles and characters, at 1 to 2 seconds a frame. Surfaces are unlit and some geometry is missing. It lists nearly all of the world's shaders as translated.

AnyXboxX now runs victory-fork with seven of that project's open pull requests added. Its maintainer measures about 5.4 frames a second on an RTX 4070 SUPER and calls it the best picture so far. An earlier mix reached about 6.6 with a setting since turned off, after a report that it makes characters' skin disappear.

Open pull requests on victory-fork report it on AMD cards for the first time: 15 minutes in the first scene at 3.4 to 4.3 frames a second on an RX 7800 XT, and the world drawn on an RX 7900 XT. These are their authors' own measurements. One measures 5 to 8 seconds a frame under Linux.

palmetto's repository stopped answering at about 21:50 UTC. Its last commit, at 21:29 UTC, added a content policy and a contact path for rights holders. No published takedown notice names it, and the reason is not known.

updates.title: Palmwave drops its XCL-based code for a renamed copy of the fork
points: At 21:12 UTC Palmwave replaced its main branch with a single commit whose files match victory-fork's one for one, with the names changed. Its README now repeats the fork's status table and figures, and names neither VIctory nor the fork.
Its XCL-based work, which an hour earlier had drawn the first mission's world into its buffers, is no longer on that branch.
It gives no measurements of its own on the new code, so it moves from the standings to the watch list.

updates.title: The press reports the Take-Two notice; five-star-recomp's cutscene reaches 30 frames a second
points: GameRiv has reported GitHub's publication of the Take-Two notice against Leonida and its forks. It quotes no statement from Take-Two, Rockstar or GitHub.

five-star-recomp now plays the opening cutscene's art, credit cards, dialogue and sound at a steady 30 frames a second, up from about 1.5, after removing a slow memory query from its busiest code. The cutscene's 3D world does not draw yet.
XCL merged a fix for a freeze about 180 seconds into the world. Its status line is unchanged.

updates.title: Correction: the build listed as hyphennn is the fork itself, now named victory-fork
points: PortWatch now says the private build it listed as hyphennn is the fork's own, shown on its developer's live streams. The separate entry added here at 20:51 UTC is withdrawn and merged into the fork's.
The fork has been renamed from victory-gta6 to victory-fork. Its old address redirects.
PortWatch reports those streams showing the first gameplay scene with ray-traced lighting, detailed textures and hair at about 3 frames a second. The fork's README still lists shadows as black.

updates.title: Longer and faster runs on the fork; Palmwave draws the world
points: AnyXboxX now measures up to 5.4 frames a second on the fork, on an RTX 4070 SUPER. Its notes relay a third-party report of 21.5 minutes without a fault on an RTX 4060 Ti, which neither AnyXboxX nor this page has checked.

Palmwave, on XCL's code, now draws the first mission's world into its internal buffers: street, ground, trees, people and a car, shown through a debug view under a fixed light. The picture the game presents is still almost one dark colour, at 2 to 5 seconds a frame, with several passes patched off.
Palmwave moves ahead of XCL, whose own status line still says gameplay is not reached.

updates.title: The fork drops the game's name as more builds pile onto it
points: victory-gta6 removed the game's name from its code and documents at 20:45 UTC; they now say "the title". Its address is unchanged. Take-Two's notice against Leonida had pointed to that project's explicit focus on the game.
The fork also merged an outside fix that lets the shaders behind its indirect lighting translate. Its README has not yet said whether shadows are now lit.

PortWatch lists a second private build on the fork, by a developer it calls hyphennn and shown on live streams: under player control in the opening scenes, with better lighting than other builds and no measured frame rate.
five-star-recomp, which has its own code, now finishes the story load and starts the opening cutscene, at under 2 frames a second.

updates.title: A third build runs on the fork, at about 5 frames a second
points: PortWatch reports a private build by a developer it calls omonkey, built on victory-gta6 and shown on live streams: about 5 frames a second in the opening prison scene, with a player walking around slowly. It has no public code.
PortWatch now ranks victory-gta6 first among projects with public code, and calls its claim self-reported.
victory-gta6's README now gives 2.5 to 4 frames a second, after clean-up passes that removed about 43% of the instructions in its translated shaders.

five-star-recomp's story load now runs a full 300 seconds without a fault, though it does not finish. palmetto's presented frames are black, which its notes trace to textures not yet filled from the game's memory.

updates.title: A second developer confirms the fork: 13 minutes of play at about 4 frames a second
points: AnyXboxX has switched to the victory-gta6 fork. Its maintainer reports playing for about 13 minutes at about 4 frames a second on an RTX 4070 SUPER, with the world on screen, the character under control and the first characters answering.
The session ended when the graphics device was lost, and an earlier cold start crashed while loading. The fork's own README says a device loss in its newest commits has since been traced and fixed.
That is the first confirmation of the fork's claim from a second machine. The fork moves to first place, ahead of the private CGBJ build, and AnyXboxX to second.
The time-to-playable estimate comes in by a day, to about 3 days. The one notice GitHub published since the last check concerns an unrelated project.

updates.title: palmetto presents its first frames
points: palmetto, a solo continuation of Leonida, now executes the game's draws without a graphics fault and presents frames in a window, measured over a 150-second run. It moves from the watch list into the standings at stage 4.
The maintainer's notes say the data behind those draws is still a stand-in, so no picture of the game is claimed.
five-star-recomp now loads the game's saved settings, so later boots skip the first-run screens and reach the story load in about 39 seconds.
No new takedown notice has appeared, and all 19 repositories this page tests still answer. victory-gta6's claim has no outside confirmation yet.

updates.title: A public VIctory fork reports the first gameplay scene with textures and sunlight
points: victory-gta6, a fork of VIctory first published at 18:02 UTC, says in its README that the game's first gameplay scene renders with characters, textures, sky and sunlit surfaces, and that the HUD, pause menu and controller input work.

It measures 2 to 4 frames a second on an RTX 4070, against 3 to 6 seconds a frame when the work began. Everything the sun does not hit directly is black, because the game's ray-traced lighting does not run yet.

The claim is unverified: one machine, no pictures, and the README says its newest commits lose the graphics device shortly after start. It enters the standings second, behind CGBJ, whose in-game state a third party has checked.
It is the first public code to claim a textured view of the world. The community project list found it.

updates.title: XCL moves to a new GitHub organisation; the press has yet to report the notice
points: XCL's repository now sits under an organisation account, xcl-dev, and its old address redirects there. Nothing in the repository says when or why it moved.

GameGPU reports a post on X, which it attributes to XCL's creator, saying Rockstar and Discord are moving against the project and that a private backup chat server exists. That is a claim, and nothing confirms it.
PC Gamer reports that at least two of Leonida's leads have quit, while others try to carry the work on. No outlet found by 19:10 UTC had reported the GitHub notice itself.
five-star-recomp traced runaway loops in two of its three stuck compute programs to a translator bug and fixed it.

updates.title: GitHub publishes a Take-Two takedown notice against Leonida and its forks
points: GitHub's public list of takedown notices now carries one from Take-Two, dated 24 November, against Leonida's repository. GitHub says it applied it to the whole fork network, 3,007 repositories.

It is the first notice to name a GTA VI project. Take-Two calls the leaked build stolen game files and argues that a project made to run it facilitates infringement even when users supply the files themselves.
The four Leonida forks this page watched all stopped answering between 18:11 and 18:30 UTC. Two continuations of its code that are not GitHub forks still answer.
No notice names VIctory, XCL or any other project in the standings, and all of them still answer.

updates.title: g6shim reaches the account picker; palmetto records its draws
points: g6shim's README says its target title now renders at about 12 frames a second up to its account picker. It moves from the watch list into the standings at stage 5.
palmetto now builds all 10,241 of the game's graphics pipelines and records about 42,700 draws in a 150-second run. None of the draws executes yet, and no frame is presented.
XCL has merged the start of a shader path that writes DXIL directly, without the standard compiler. five-star-recomp has an optional one of its own, which it measures at 5 to 20 times faster.

updates.title: five-star-recomp fixes its memory corruption
points: five-star-recomp says the memory corruption in its story load is fixed. A translator bug had made a culling pass write its counts to the wrong place, and a boot now runs past 200 seconds.
Its new stop is the game's own hang check, at about 200 seconds, because graphics frames take too long during the load. Three compute programs still run their loops to the safety cap.
An open VIctory pull request ports XCL's way of running 64-lane compute shaders on cards with 32 lanes. It is a first cut, off by default, and claims no in-game result.

VIctory's main branch has had no commit since 09:53 UTC, while more than 1,000 pull requests have been opened against it. Contributors are now bundling groups of them and testing the bundles together.

updates.title: AnyXboxX measures 3.2 frames a second and narrows down the black picture
points: AnyXboxX's notes for the evening of 24 November give about 3.2 frames a second in the world when the game runs in its Series S mode, which renders at 1280x720, against 2.0 to 2.4 in Series X mode. Both are on its local branch, on an RTX 4070 SUPER.
The same notes say the world's geometry and the cutscene's characters are present in internal buffers, while the final picture is one flat tint that darkens over time, with subtitles on top.
The cause it gives: about 379 draw calls start with empty arguments, because the graphics passes that fill them in are not translated yet.
five-star-recomp has named the pass that writes over game memory during its story load, an instance-culling pass. Its notes say the fault is not fixed yet.

updates.title: A VIctory pull request holds the world for six minutes on an NVIDIA card
points: An open VIctory pull request reports more than 6 minutes in game without a crash on an NVIDIA RTX 4080 Super, with the settings menu opening. Before it, the same card lost its graphics device within 10 seconds of entering the world.

The change marks the game's 64-lane shaders so that a card with 32 lanes refuses them cleanly, where before they ran, looped forever and hung the card. The pull request does not say what the picture shows.
Another open pull request stops graphics memory filling up on Linux, which had ended runs after a few minutes in the world. Use fell from 15 GB to about 4.6 GB.

Late addition: PortWatch reported early on 24 November that XCL told it the game runs at 30 frames a second in game, without saying whether that means menus or gameplay. XCL's README still says gameplay is not reached, and PortWatch has not moved XCL up.

updates.title: Palmwave narrows its claim
points: Palmwave's rewritten status says only part of the world's geometry is drawn: poles, power lines, fences and bike racks, with about 91% of the depth buffer still empty. The entry here at 15:51 said the street was drawn.
Its world frames now take about 10 seconds, lighting shows in about 1.5% of its target, and it has not tested controls in the world.
AnyXboxX's author has sent the change behind its tenfold speed gain to VIctory as a pull request.

updates.title: five-star-recomp gets past the game's hang check
points: five-star-recomp says the game's 30-second hang check no longer ends its story load, and a memory blow-up from the graphics driver's shader compiler is contained. Runs now stop about 130 seconds in, when graphics work corrupts game memory again.
XCL's main branch is taking merges again after two quiet hours. Its status line has not changed.
VGC and Eurogamer now cover Leonida's shutdown. Rockstar and Take-Two have still said nothing, and no takedown notice names a GTA VI project.

updates.title: AnyXboxX reports a controllable character; Palmwave draws the world's geometry
points: AnyXboxX says a local branch reaches the world with a controllable character. The game's movement tutorial shows over a 3D image that is still black.

That branch runs at about 2.4 frames a second on an RTX 4070 SUPER, up from 0.2 this morning, after it removed several per-frame costs. About 170 shaders are still untranslated in game, down from 456.

Palmwave now draws the first mission's street into its internal buffers and stays in the world for 3 minutes. Its screen is still one flat colour, because the lighting passes run out of order, and a frame takes 12 to 19 seconds.
AnyXboxX moves to stage 6. Three builds now report the game world under control or on screen: one private, one in an open pull request, and this one.

updates.title: A lit, textured scene on a Mac; public code reports a player walking
points: A Reddit post shows a VIctory build running under CrossOver on an M5 Max Mac: bare grey geometry at 4 frames a second, then about six hours later a textured, sunlit prison yard with characters. Its author says matching the console's picture is proving hard.

An open VIctory pull request reports a similar view from public code. Under Proton on Linux the world ran 8 minutes without a graphics fault, its geometry showed through a debug view, and a player could walk the first mission's street.
VIctory moves to stage 6 on that report. Its own README has not changed and still calls the scene dark.
The estimate moves in by half a day, to about the morning of Sat 28 Nov.

updates.title: five-star-recomp clears its memory fault; press reports more chat servers gone
points: five-star-recomp says the memory corruption and graphics hangs in its story load are fixed. The game now ends itself late in the load, most likely through its own hang check while shaders are still compiling.
VGTimes reports that the VIctory team's Discord server was blocked, without saying by whom, and that XCL's team deleted its own group chat. Rockstar has not commented.
VIctory's public repository has had no commit since 09:53 UTC, while the private build based on it moves ahead.

updates.title: Three more projects on the watch list
points: Two continuations of Leonida are active. One keeps its full history and says the game does not boot yet. The other, palmetto, reports the game reaching its own render code on an RTX 4090 with no frame.
g6shim, a new set of replacement system libraries, reports the game starting and stopping where graphics begin.
Nothing changed at the front in the last 20 minutes.

updates.title: A private build is in the game world with a player moving
points: PortWatch reports that CGBJ, a private group building on VIctory with some of XCL's work, has the game in its world. A player can walk, talk to characters and open the menu.
It is far from playable. A 77-second video shows the opening scenes in flat colours without lighting, the run with walking had a black screen, and it runs very slowly.
PortWatch says it checked that the build gets in game. The code is private, so nobody outside the group can test it, and no public project has shown a player moving.
The estimate now marks in-game as reached. Playable stays at about the evening of Sat 28 Nov.

updates.title: five-star-recomp reaches the story intro's title card
points: On one run, five-star-recomp loaded story mode and showed the story intro's title card before stopping. Its other runs stop earlier.
Its notes blame graphics work that writes past its buffers into the game's own memory, probably because the console's bounds checks are not applied yet.
Three separate code bases have now shown that card: VIctory's, XCL's through Palmwave, and five-star-recomp's. None of them draws the scene after it in public code.

updates.title: Press names a private build behind the in-game footage
points: DSOGaming reports that a private build called CGBJ, based on VIctory with some of XCL's work, has reached in-game. It has no public code or download.
That matches the stream footage logged at 11:10 UTC, which X accounts had described as the VIctory team's. Which description is right is not settled.
No public repository shows a visible world yet. Palmwave's copy of XCL now decodes the game's textures, and it is still chasing the bad geometry behind its blank frames.
GamesRadar now covers Leonida's shutdown. No outlet reports a statement from Rockstar or Take-Two, and reports of wider Discord takedowns rest on Reddit posts.

updates.title: Palmwave shows the first mission's opening card
points: Palmwave now presents the first mission's opening card, its text over a plain background, before world frames that are still a single flat colour.
Its notes trace the empty picture to the world's geometry. Through XCL's mesh path the depth buffer receives thin needle-shaped triangles in place of the scene.
five-star-recomp now decodes every one of the game's texture formats exactly, given decoding tables the user supplies, and its loader hands the game real texture data in place of placeholders.
VIctory has had no commit for two hours, and the stream footage of a lit scene is still unconfirmed by any repository.

updates.title: Palmwave puts world frames on screen, with nothing in them yet
points: Palmwave, the XCL fork, now loads the world in about 84 seconds and presents its frames. The picture is a flat background colour, and each frame takes from 18 seconds to 2 minutes of graphics work.
It got there on an RTX 5080 with the game's hang check and two of its lighting passes patched off, and with shaders cached from earlier runs.
Its notes blame the slowness on 4.4 GB of the game's graphics memory sitting in system memory, where one pass took 431 ms against 0.45 ms in video memory.
No repository has confirmed the footage of a lit scene from the VIctory stream, and VIctory's README is unchanged.

updates.title: Reports of limits on the projects' chat servers and streams
points: X accounts following the projects say VIctory's Discord server was banned and its stream on Kick was ended, and that the team now streams elsewhere. Neither VIctory nor the press has confirmed this.
XCL's Discord is closed to new members. A moderator's message relayed on X says Discord limited the server.
Every tracked GitHub repository still answers, and GitHub lists no notice against any of them.

updates.title: Footage shows a partly lit scene from the game
points: A clip relayed on X from a live stream shows a dim interior with a character in it, at about 3 frames a second. Accounts following the projects say the stream is the VIctory team's, and VideoCardz also reports first 3D scenes.
No project's repository reports this yet, and VIctory's README still calls the scene dark. Treat it as unverified.
The in-game step of the estimate moves in to about a day. The playable estimate is unchanged.

updates.title: XCL takes on VIctory's texture decoder
points: XCL merged decoding for six of the console's compressed texture formats at 10:38 UTC. Its notes say the code is a port of VIctory's, used with that author's permission.
XCL's own status line is unchanged: gameplay not reached, and its fix for the refused mesh pipelines is still an open pull request.
