Kotaku now covers the race. No outlet reports a statement from Rockstar or Take-Two about these projects, and GitHub lists no notice against any of them.

updates.title: A VIctory build stays in the world for 5 minutes
points: AnyXboxX now builds on VIctory, with 24 of VIctory's open community pull requests added. On an RTX 4070 SUPER it reports the first cutscene's opening credits and 5 minutes in the world without a graphics hang.
The picture is still black. AnyXboxX says the 3D scene is drawn internally, but the lighting steps are not translated yet and the world runs at 0.3 to 0.5 frames a second.
five-star-recomp is past its graphics hang. Capping shader loops that never ended let the story load run on, and it now stops on corrupted game memory.
AnyXboxX joins the standings in second place, behind VIctory, whose code produces the result.

updates.title: VIctory's results reproduced on a second PC
points: The author of AnyXboxX ran VIctory on an RTX 4070 SUPER and measured the menus, the first-run screens, the first mission's title card and the pause menu at 30 frames a second.
In the world that run drew 1 to 2 frames a second and the graphics card hung after about 2 minutes. It counted 351 shader programs VIctory does not translate yet.
VIctory's maintainer went back to shader work at 09:53 UTC. The commit says 108 of the game's 26,096 shader programs now get past one console loop pattern and stop on a later one.
Xbox2Windows merged decoding for two compressed texture formats that it had been filling with blanks. It reports no new run.

updates.title: Estimate moves back half a day
points: The best estimate to playable moves to about 4½ days, around the evening of Sat 28 Nov, and the odds for Thursday drop to 2 in 10.
No project has drawn the world in the ten hours since the first one got inside it. Three code bases are stopped at its first frame, each for a reason it has identified.
Legal pressure is rising: one project's creator says Rockstar had its Discord server taken down, and two other projects have started to protect themselves.

updates.title: XCL spells out what its repository does not contain
points: XCL's maintainer rewrote the top of its README to say it works only on game files the user already owns, and holds no console SDK code, keys, game data or anything for getting round copy protection.
No project changed stage. No takedown notice names a GTA VI project.

updates.title: PercyScarlett withdraws its screenshots
points: About 20 minutes after publishing them, PercyScarlett removed its screenshots and the game's name from its repository. Its description of how far it gets is unchanged.
VIctory's maintainer has merged about 50 fixes from outside contributors since 07:46 UTC. Its status is unchanged.

updates.title: PercyScarlett shows the setup screens, with screenshots
points: PercyScarlett now shows the account picker, the intro video in full colour and the first-time setup screens on an unmodified executable. It published screenshots; the one this page checked shows the brightness screen with some letters missing from its text.
It moves from stage 4 to stage 5, in sixth place. Nine projects now show a picture from the game.
VIctory's maintainer merged about 30 fixes from outside contributors in half an hour. Its status is unchanged.

updates.title: Leonida's creator says Rockstar had its Discord taken down
points: Press reports say Leonida's creator wrote that Rockstar had the project's Discord server taken down, and that this was only part of the reason for stepping away. Rockstar has not commented.
GitHub's published complaints still show nothing against Leonida, and reports suggest its owners removed the repository themselves.
Claims on Reddit that other GTA VI Discord servers are being targeted are unconfirmed.
VIctory's maintainer is active again after about seven hours, merging fixes from outside contributors.

updates.title: Xbox2Windows qualifies its result
points: Xbox2Windows now says its run to the loading screen used a modified diagnostic copy of the executable and a debugger set to continue past assertions. Start-up of the original executable is unverified.
It moves down one place, behind OpenScarlett (Community Edition), which reports its result on an unmodified executable.

updates.title: Three code bases are at the first frame of the world
points: Palmwave now loads the world and keeps running for up to an hour with sound, with the game's hang check switched off. It shows nothing after loading while the world's compute shaders compile, a few of which take up to 30 minutes each.
five-star-recomp has traced its hang to the first frame after loading, at the game's meshlet culling step.

A second project called OpenScarlett, from OpenCommunityEdition, joins the standings in sixth. It runs a retail game it does not name through its first screens and intro video, then stops as the scene behind the menus streams in.
VIctory, the only project to have shown a picture inside the world, has had no commit since 00:57 UTC.

updates.title: OpenScarlett plays the game's video
points: OpenScarlett's newest commit reports the game's video playing in full colour at 4K, after its interface. It moves to sixth on its own.
G6Recomp, which could not start the game before, now gets as far as creating its window. It reuses memory code from Leonida, with credit.

updates.title: Xbox2Windows gets through setup and into loading
points: Xbox2Windows now plays the intro video, accepts the first-run setup pages and enters loading on an RTX 4060 laptop. Navigating the menus by hand is still unverified.
Four code bases have now reached loading or beyond: VIctory, XCL with its fork Palmwave, five-star-recomp and Xbox2Windows. Only VIctory is inside the world, and nobody has drawn it.

updates.title: five-star-recomp starts loading story mode
points: five-star-recomp now shows the game's logo, intro art and every first-run screen, saves its settings and starts loading story mode. About six minutes into that load the graphics card hangs. It moves back up to fourth.
Odds of a playable build by Christmas go from 8 in 10 to 7 in 10, and the chance of a stall rises to 2 in 10. The estimated date is unchanged.
The reason is a precedent: on 18 November GitHub published four Take-Two takedown notices against unofficial GTA V ports and their forks, including ports that needed the user's own game files.

updates.title: Xbox2Windows reaches the first setup pages
points: Xbox2Windows now presents the intro video and reaches the game's first setup pages, for narration and text size, on an RTX 4060 laptop. It moves up to fourth.
A change to how it runs one kind of loop took its intro video from about 14 to 30 frames a second.

updates.title: OpenScarlett reports the game's interface on screen
points: OpenScarlett's newest commits report the game passing all of its start-up tasks and drawing its interface at 4K and 30 frames a second on a 4 GB GTX 1650 Ti. It moves to stage 5.
Eight projects now show a picture from the game. One of them, VIctory, is inside the world, and none has drawn it.

updates.title: Xbox2Windows documents its start-up run
points: Xbox2Windows now carries the earlier contributor report in its own documentation as a measured result: about 29 frames a second, the interface drawn, the first-run prompt answered and the intro video playing with wrong colours. It stops in texture streaming and moves up to fifth.
XCL merged six more changes, among them building pipelines an earlier run used before they are needed. Its status line is unchanged.
VIctory has had no commit since 00:57 UTC.

updates.title: GTA6-BootTest joins the standings
points: GTA6-BootTest, a project this page had missed, boots the game and draws its first interface screen through translated shaders. It joins at stage 5, in sixth place.
five-star-recomp now runs for three minutes without a crash, with real images on screen, while the game is still loading.
A community project list reports that a second, smaller project, americas-recomp, went offline on 23 November shortly before Leonida. No cause is given for either.

updates.title: Xbox2Windows reports a visible intro
points: Xbox2Windows: a contributor reports a visible intro video on an RX 9070 XT, with wrong colours and black frames after it. The project moves from stage 3 to stage 5, in sixth place, and has not yet checked a frame against a reference.
five-star-recomp is past the assert that stopped it and now streams the game's next stage, compressed textures included. It stops at one texture layout method it has not implemented yet.
Six projects now show a picture from the game. None has drawn the world.

updates.title: Estimate moves back a day
points: The best estimate to playable moves from about 3 days to about 4, around Sat 28 Nov. Nobody has drawn the world in the three and a half hours since the first project got inside it, and frame times there are ten times or more too slow.
Palmwave now loads the world at 5 to 30 frames a second with memory levelling off. It stops as the world starts to draw, when the game's watchdog ends a wait for pipelines still compiling.
five-star-recomp added a disk pipeline cache. VIctory and XCL's main branch have had no substantive change for about two hours.
Press coverage has started: outlets report the game reaching its settings and legal screens on PC, with nothing playable.

updates.title: Two of Leonida's forks are gone
points: Two of the four contributor forks of Leonida that this page watches stopped answering between 00:19 and 01:37 UTC. The cause is not known, and no takedown notice naming the project has been published.
five-star-recomp's first image now shows in the right colours after a fix to 61 pipelines.
No project changed stage.

updates.title: five-star-recomp draws its first picture
points: five-star-recomp: the game's interface layer and intro video now draw, its first image after hours of black frames. It moves to stage 5 and fourth place.
An assert inside the game still stops it shortly after, and one drawing fix is being merged.
XCL merged a change that skips uploading textures whose memory has not changed. Its status line is unchanged.
Five projects now show a picture from the game. None has drawn the world.

updates.title: Three more projects report start-up progress
points: Palmwave, a fork of XCL, measures a retail game it does not name into world loading on an RTX 5080: 0 to 2 frames a second, with memory growing until the run is stopped at 140 seconds. It joins the standings in third.
Its own fix lifts the intro video from 3.5 to about 19 frames a second. It reports that compressed world textures are not decoded yet in this code.
Xbox2Windows says local runs of the main executable now reach graphics pipeline creation, its first report of running the title's own code. No rendered frame is verified.
Holy-Interoperability presents its first frame of a retail title it does not name, then stops in start-up.

updates.title: XCL's code is measured on a second PC
points: Palmwave, now built on XCL's code, measured a retail game it does not name on an RTX 5080. It shows first screens at up to 30 frames a second, slows to about 3 frames a second, then crashes as memory grows while the world loads.
Its list of what separates that code from playable: memory growth in world loading, which XCL has since fixed, texture decoding failures, refused mesh pipelines and a slow phase with no known cause.
TuxBox: shader preparation now compiles 2,755 of 11,429 requests captured from its runs. Its picture is unchanged at the player-selection prompt.
VIctory merged 11 fixes from outside contributors in half an hour. Its status is unchanged.

updates.title: VIctory draws the first mission's title card
points: VIctory: after the world loads, the first mission's title card now renders. It is the first picture past the loading screen that any project on this page has reported.
The scene after the card is still dark, at 0.5 to 1.8 seconds a frame, and runs end on a graphics fault within about 55 seconds.
five-star-recomp: the game now reads input, starts its save system and pairs a gamepad after a scripted button press. Frames are still black, and an assert inside the game stops it there.
Palmwave has switched to XCL's code. XCL's own status line is unchanged, and Leonida is still unreachable.

updates.title: Leonida halts: its lead steps away and its repository is gone
points: Leonida's lead posted a decision to step away. Its GitHub repository no longer exists at either address, its own mirror server is down, and its chat is reported gone.

Whether a takedown was involved is not known. GitHub shows a notice page for repositories removed on a copyright complaint and has published none; contributors' forks and the lead's other repository are still up.
The projects ahead of it are unaffected: VIctory, XCL, TuxBox and five-star-recomp were all reachable at 23:56 UTC.

updates.title: Leonida's GitHub repository is unreachable again
points: Leonida: its GitHub repository stopped answering between 23:31 and 23:48 UTC, at both its new address and its old one. The cause is not known. The earlier gap tonight was a move, and contributors' forks, the owner's other repository and the project's own mirror are all still up. No takedown notice is published.
VIctory: two more outside fixes merged. The world is still black at 1.5 to 3 seconds a frame.

updates.title: VIctory keeps the game world running, still black
points: VIctory: a 23:13 UTC commit fixes the graphics-device failure. The world ran to a four-minute limit. The picture is black, at 1.5 to 3 seconds a frame.
By its notes, most of the world's geometry is drawn through a path that is switched off for now, and hundreds of draws a frame have no translated shader.
XCL: merged another batch, including the intro-video fix. Its status is unchanged.

updates.title: XCL merges its world-loading fix
points: XCL: the fix for storage requests that failed while the world loads is on the main branch since 22:54 UTC. No picture of the world is reported yet.
VIctory: a contributor's change gets the game past start-up on Intel processors, tested on a second machine. Its status is unchanged: the world loads and the picture is black.
Leonida: a pull request reports a repeating render loop that tries to present frames, and says visible frames are not verified.

updates.title: TuxBox shows the first menu on Linux
points: TuxBox: a 22:25 UTC commit shows the game's player-selection prompt at 4K on Linux. It moves to stage 5, the third project with a picture.

XCL: a contributor's pull request fixes most of the storage requests that failed while the world loads. In the contributor's 170-second run 16,384 requests now land and 2,227 still fail. Another pull request fixes the green screen where the intro video plays. Neither is merged.
VIctory: no commits since 22:15 UTC. Leonida: merging pull requests again at its new address.

updates.title: A new leader: VIctory loads the game world, with a black picture
points: VIctory, a one-person project published today, reports the game running through its first-boot screens, intro video and menus at 30 frames a second, then loading the world in about 50 seconds. In the world the picture is black and the graphics device fails within seconds. Tested on one machine.
It stays at stage 5: stage 6 needs a picture of the world and player control.

Correction on Leonida: its repository was not taken down. The maintainer moved it to a GitHub organisation at about 22:10 UTC, and the old address stopped answering for a few minutes. Pull requests are being merged again.
This page was redesigned at 22:33 UTC.

updates.title: Leonida's GitHub repository goes dark; XCL reaches the settings screens
points: Leonida: the GitHub repository answered at 22:08 UTC and no longer did at 22:12. It now responds like a repository that is missing or private. The cause is not known. Several contributors' forks, the owner's other repository and every other project on this page were still reachable at 22:16 UTC, and GitHub has published no notice.
Leonida's own mirror is still up with the same history, last commit 21:01 UTC. This page now reads Leonida from there.
XCL: the main branch goes past the first menu into the settings screens at a steady 30 frames per second, with memory use down to about 15 GB. Its status line says gameplay has not been reached.
Forecast unchanged for now. A confirmed takedown would push it out.

updates.title: No change at the front
points: XCL: main branch unchanged since 21:30 UTC. In chat, the contributor who reached the menus says world loading stalls because most storage requests fail. No pull request for that yet.
PercyScarlett fixed an early device removal. five-star-recomp ruled out network access as the reason the game idles. TuxBox and OpenScarlett edged forward. None reports a picture.

updates.title: Chat report: an XCL build gets through the menus and starts loading the game
points: XCL: the contributor behind the first-menus pull request said in the project's chat at 21:36 UTC that the contributor's build now saves preferences, selects a player and begins loading into the main game. The contributor's earlier menu report was confirmed on the main branch within about half an hour.
This is a chat message, not a commit or pull request, and it does not claim a frame of the game world or player control. XCL stays at stage 5.
Forecast: the in-game step is brought forward to about a day. The playable date is unchanged.

updates.title: A sixth project presents frames; no new milestone at the front
points: PercyScarlett: reaches the game's frame loop and first present with black frames, then a GPU hang about 5 seconds in. Added to the standings at stage 4.

XCL: about 35 more commits merged, including a fix for the menus' missing body text. Its status is unchanged: first menu at 30 frames per second, nothing checked past it. A pull request for the mesh pipelines its minimap needs is open.
five-star-recomp: now reads its black frames as the game's own fade from black while it waits on something.
OpenScarlett: two more boot obstacles cleared and more than 360 frames at 4K without a crash on a 4 GB graphics card. No picture described.

updates.title: No new milestone; XCL merges fast behind its first menu
points: XCL: eleven pull requests merged at 20:49 to 20:50 UTC and review fixes at 20:56. Two new pull requests go at the known gaps: one for the missing menu text, one for the mesh-shader slot that the main branch refuses. Neither is merged.
Leonida: a correction. Its README now lists the project's own server as a mirror of the repository, so this is a mirror for now, not a move. Both copies match.
five-star-recomp, OpenScarlett and TuxBox: no change. Palmwave no longer names the game in its README.

updates.title: XCL's main branch shows the first menu at 30 frames per second
points: XCL: a 20:47 UTC commit by the maintainer puts the first menu on the main branch. The account prompt is visible at a steady 30 frames per second with no crash, on a 16 GB graphics card. It uses parts of the earlier pull request and its own memory handling. Nothing past that menu has been checked on main.
five-star-recomp: start-up loading completes and the game then idles on an early screen, still black.
OpenScarlett: reports the first frame's three draws executing and boot moving on into render-graph set-up. No picture described.
Leonida: its main branch on GitHub moved again at 20:34 UTC with two commits from the maintainer. The copy on its new server followed within a minute.
Forecast unchanged at about 3 days. The low frame rate seen in the earlier pull request does not appear on the main branch.

updates.title: Leonida's official repository appears on its new server
points: Leonida: the official repository is now on the project's own server. For now it is a copy of the GitHub repository with the same main branch, still the 18:54 UTC commit. This page watches both.
XCL: the first-menus pull request is still open and unmerged. A second contributor's rectangle-list fix already tests against what that build reported. Main branch unchanged since 18:11 UTC.
Palmwave reaches its first console command list. five-star-recomp, TuxBox and OpenScarlett: no change.

updates.title: XCL: a pull request reports the game's first menus on screen
points: XCL: a contributor's pull request, opened at 20:15 UTC on top of the main branch, reports the account prompt and the legal menus on screen after about 45 seconds of black frames, navigable with a gamepad. A four-minute run did not crash. XCL moves to stage 5.

Its limits, by its own description: one machine with a top-end graphics card, most letters missing from the menu body text, 7 to 28 frames per second in the menus, tests not run, and nothing seen past the menus. It is not merged or reviewed.
The video noted in the last update matches it. The pull request says one later screen came out as a single solid colour, and that colour is the exact green seen in the video.
Forecast pulled in to about 3 days.

updates.title: Leonida is further on than its main branch shows
points: Leonida: pull requests that are still waiting to be merged show one contributor's build reaching the game's frame loop, with black frames and stand-in pipelines, and another working out why the first interface draw shows nothing. Leonida moves to stage 4. This page now reads Leonida's open pull requests as well as its main branch.

Leonida: a pull request adds a notice that the project is moving its git hosting to its own server. The official repository was not there yet at 20:10 UTC. The main branch on GitHub has merged nothing since 18:54 UTC.

five-star-recomp: rectangle lists fixed and the frame loop is now stable at 30 frames per second in two-minute runs. Frames are still black, and the project says the game is waiting in an early splash or loading state.

Unverified sighting: a screen-share video shows a near-empty first screen with controller prompts, a plain green screen for a few seconds, then the game's legal notices menu. The details fit a real early boot, including Xbox prompts and the green of a movie playing with empty frames. No repository has claimed it, so no project is credited and no stage moves.
XCL: no commits on its main branch since 18:11 UTC.

updates.title: Leonida's main branch has stopped merging; a menu clip is unconfirmed
points: Leonida: no merges into the main branch since 18:54 UTC, after an earlier gap from 17:23 to 18:20. New pull requests keep arriving at several hundred an hour, and their numbers have passed 8,900 while the last one merged is near 6,530. This page reads the main branch, so Leonida may be further on than shown.
People in the project chats say GitHub is rate limiting Leonida and that it may move its git hosting. Nothing in its repository or on its website confirms a move yet.

Unconfirmed: a clip said to show the game's legal notices screen running on a PC is being passed around project chats. No repository reports a visible picture yet, and a clip with the same screens posted on 19 November was shown to be fake. It is not counted here.
XCL and five-star-recomp: no change. Both still run the frame loop on a black screen.

updates.title: Five projects added to the watch list
points: Added after a wider search: AnyXboxX, Palmwave, PercyScarlett, G6Recomp and Holy-Interoperability. None has shown the game running.
XCL: a user in its issue tracker reports reproducing the 30 frames per second run on the latest commit, 6,557 frames over 231 seconds, ending in an assert. Nobody there reports a visible picture.
No project has published a menu, a logo or any visible picture from the game.

updates.title: five-star-recomp draws level with XCL
points: five-star-recomp: the game now presents frames continuously, about 27,000 in a two-minute run. Every frame is black. The project lists the causes it knows: rectangle lists drawn as one triangle, render-target states and many views.
XCL: no commits since 18:11. It runs the same loop at a steady 30 frames per second, also black.
XValkyrie: a commit adds what a newer-kit title needs on the way to its first frame. It names no game and states no result.
Forecast pulled in by a day, to about 4 days.

updates.title: OpenScarlett presents too, making four
points: OpenScarlett: a commit reports 34 boot obstacles cleared, up from 17, and the game presenting to a 4K window. It does not describe the picture.
five-star-recomp: the first frame now records its work with real pipelines and bound descriptors. The graphics card then hangs before a second frame.
XCL: no commits since 18:11. Leonida: active, with no change to its boot notes.

updates.title: Three projects now present frames
points: five-star-recomp: the game's first present now appears in its own window through a swap chain. Nothing is drawn, and the game then stops in the graphics driver. The project also has a first version of placing textures at the game's own GPU addresses.
XCL: no commits since 18:11.
Leonida: merging to its main branch has resumed, with no change to its boot notes.

updates.title: XCL holds 30 fps on a black screen
points: XCL: the game now runs at a steady 30 frames per second, 1,449 frames in a 60-second test with no crash. The picture is black. Its command lists now really execute; until this change they went through a placeholder.
TuxBox: on Linux, the game opens its window, starts audio, opens its archives and presents at 3840 by 2160. The window stays black.
Leonida: no commits to its main branch for an hour.

updates.title: five-star-recomp reaches its first present
points: five-star-recomp: the game now gets through render targets and pipelines to its first present call and into its frame loop. Nothing is drawn or shown yet. It stops in the graphics driver because descriptor heaps are not bound on command lists and resources at the game's own GPU addresses are not real yet.
XCL: no commits since 17:03. It still stops at about three minutes.
Leonida: no commits to its main branch since 17:23.

updates.title: XCL runs for about three minutes
points: XCL: the game runs about 3 minutes without a crash, up from 45 seconds. It shows two frames after about 4 seconds, loads roughly 3,500 shaders, then stops at about 183 seconds when five mesh-shader pipelines fail. The frames have not been checked.
five-star-recomp: now gets past the game's GPU-memory buffers and descriptor heaps, then stops when an invalid call removes the graphics device.
xbox-emulator: a community project list reports a contributor reaching the game window, graphics device and archives with local patches. This is second-hand; the repository has no new commits.

updates.title: A fourth project starts the game
points: five-star-recomp: the executable starts under its loader and gets through memory setup, archive opening and graphics device setup, then stops before a first frame.
OpenScarlett: its README now documents 17 cleared boot obstacles. The 587 imports it cites match the count five-star-recomp gives for GTA VI's executable.

updates.title: XCL stops crashing
points: XCL: the game runs 45 seconds without a crash. Memory use falls from 28.7 GB to 16 or 17 GB and the first frame arrives at 3.6 seconds.
OpenScarlett: reports clearing 17 early boot obstacles on a retail title, as far as a 4K render target and ray-tracing setup.

updates.title: Leonida reaches the graphics device
points: Leonida: a contributor's local build runs the executable as far as creating the graphics device and its first descriptor heap, then halts on an assert. The main branch has mapped and initialised the file.

updates.title: First frame on a PC
points: XCL: the game starts and presents a first frame after 8.3 seconds at 3840 by 2160, then runs out of memory at about 20 seconds while compiling pipelines. Nobody looked at the frame.

updates.title: The executable appears
points: The leaker known as CyberLeek publishes the game's main executable, the one file missing from the Xbox build it released on 19 November. Press reports put this about three hours before its own 17:00 UTC deadline.

notes.label: Играбельные сборки
notes.text: По собственным заявлениям, без сторонней верификации: Vice-Tay документирует 30-минутную сессию с медианой 21,1 кадра в секунду на собственном тестовом ПК. Эта страница содержит ссылки только на исходный код проектов, а не на сборки или загрузочные файлы. 26 ноября VGTimes сообщил о распространении упакованной сборки, приписываемой CGBJ, что никто не подтвердил. Загрузки, предлагаемые как GTA VI для ПК, содержат вредоносное ПО с августа.

notes.label: Сборка
notes.text: Эти проекты работают на основе утекшей сборки Xbox. В прессе 25 и 26 ноября сообщалось, что утекла и сборка для PlayStation 5; ни один из перечисленных проектов не сообщает о ее запуске на ПК. Rockstar не выпускала и не анонсировала версию для ПК. Эта страница не содержит ссылок на утечки и не объясняет, как их получить или запустить.

notes.label: Источники
notes.text: Публичные репозитории проектов, открытые пул-реквесты (PR) и, где отмечено, чаты проектов. Названия проектов ведут на соответствующие репозитории для указания авторства.

notes.label: Статус разработки
notes.text: Каждый этап — это утверждение самого проекта, если в строке источника не указано иное; большинство из них не подтверждены. Статус CGBJ основан на сообщениях прессы, так как его код закрыт.

notes.label: Частота кадров
notes.text: Отрисованные кадры. Кадры, добавленные с помощью генерации кадров, помечаются отдельно и не учитываются при достижении планки «Играбельно».

notes.label: Потоки
notes.text: Проект на 6-й или 7-й стадии оценивается по трем критериям: картинка, скорость и стабильность. Каждый шаг — это интерпретация данной страницей того, что проект сообщает о себе; ключ под заголовком рейтинга перечисляет эти шаги. Скорость — это среднее значение, которое проект сообщает за свою новейшую игровую сессию длительностью от 10 минут, или медиана, если среднее не указано. Если проект не сообщает о такой сессии, берется среднее значение из частоты кадров в игровом процессе, при этом низкие показатели учитываются, если они относятся к отрезку или условиям игры, а не к отдельным кадрам. Скриптовые или автоматизированные прогоны и сцены, где персонаж стоит на месте, не считаются игровым процессом. Если проект ведет посекундный лог сессии и не дает общего значения, скорость рассчитывается как среднее арифметическое медиан по каждой минуте. Проект, признанный играбельным (стадия 7), оценивается не по планке «Играбельно», а по следующей цели: одна игровая сессия длительностью от часа при 30 кадрах в секунду или выше (только отрендеренные кадры), что соответствует высшим ступеням по критериям скорости и стабильности.

notes.label: Протестировано на
notes.text: Системы и производители видеокарт, на которых, по заявлениям проекта или его тестеров, он запускается. Возможно, он работает и на другом оборудовании; если строка пуста, значит, данных нет.

notes.label: Отчеты о сбоях
notes.text: Согласно примечаниям одного из проектов, система отчетов о сбоях игры отправляет данные на внешний сервер при каждом вылете.

notes.label: Кто компилирует
notes.text: ИИ-ассистент (Claude), автоматически, примерно каждые 15 минут. Может ошибаться.

notes.label: Аффилированность
notes.text: Отсутствует с Rockstar Games, Take-Two Interactive, Microsoft или любым другим проектом из списка, а также с любым сайтом или инструментом, использующим данные рейтинги.

notes.label: Позиции
notes.text: Строки на 6-й и 7-й стадиях упорядочены исключительно по их критериям: наименьшее количество шагов до планки «Играбельно» (стадия 6) или до следующей цели (стадия 7) по совокупности скорости и стабильности, затем по качеству картинки, частоте кадров и длительности сессии. Более низкие стадии упорядочены по оценке того, что остается до следующей стадии. Место в рейтинге вычисляется на основе того, что проект сообщает о себе: это не является верификацией или одобрением. Знак равенства означает одинаковый уровень.

notes.label: Запросы
notes.text: Чтобы попросить добавить, исправить или удалить проект с этой страницы,
